metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Energy Market Operations Platform domain: the energy lifecycle Propose -> Onboard -> Measure -> Bill -> Serve -> Source -> Forecast -> Nominate -> Steer -> Settle as run by suppliers, BRPs, traders and large consumers on the combined Eneve platform (Energy21 EBASE, Ecedo, Jules, Gridhub and Nemon heritage), plus the market-entry and integration journeys that make a regulated, real-time market operable on one backbone.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (EDSN and the central connection register, TenneT MMC-Hub and nomination interfaces, gas TSO, ETPA, the day-ahead exchange, OMIE and REE/SIPS, smart-meter and telemetry providers, guarantees-of-origin registry, banks and payment providers, ERP, price and weather feeds, ACM/CNMC and heritage platforms) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Supplier Journeys
rootGroups.description: From idea to live proposition, from sign-up to active supply, and from meter data to a correct, paid invoice served through the supplier's own brand: the journeys of the Supplier Suite that put the connection, contract, volume and invoice at the heart of the platform.

streams.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streams.description: Take an energy proposition from idea to live product in weeks: commercial teams configure products, tariffs, pricing logic, sign-up journeys, campaigns and sales-channel availability in the low-code proposition builder, and every configured product plugs into contracts, billing, portal and settlement automatically instead of waiting for an eighteen-month build.
outcomes: New propositions go live in weeks rather than the eighteen months that lets competitors land first, because product, tariff, journey and campaign are configured, not built
Every configured product plugs into the order-to-cash backbone automatically, so no launch needs a parallel billing workaround
Dynamic, EV time-of-use, battery, capacity-linked and bundled offers are priced from the same curves the portfolio desk uses, so launched margins are the margins the CFO sees
Commercial teams switch campaigns and channels on and off without an IT release

flows.title: Configure and Launch a Dynamic Tariff Proposition
flows.description: The Proposition and Pricing Manager (prop) configures a spot-linked dynamic tariff with an EV time-of-use variant, validates it against billing with the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo), gets approval from the Energy Company Director (exec) and monitors conversion after launch.
flows.trigger: The commercial team decides to launch a dynamic tariff before the next quarter and opens the proposition builder.
flows.successSignal: The proposition is available in the chosen channels, the first sign-ups create contracts and the first invoices bill correctly without a manual step.

steps.title: Define the product and contract type
keyFacts: The builder supports every contract and product type in the Supplier Suite: fixed, variable, dynamic, EV, battery and bundled offers as well as complex B2B multi-site agreements.
A dynamic tariff is defined as a formula over the day-ahead price per 15-minute block plus configured mark-ups, taxes and fees rather than as code.
painPoints: Product definitions that live in a billing engine's configuration are invisible to marketing and cannot be reviewed by non-technical staff.
A contract type that is not modelled up front forces a manual billing exception for every customer on it.

steps.title: Model pricing logic and expected margin
keyFacts: Pricing logic references the portfolio's price curves and cost-plus components so that the launched margin is consistent with the sourcing desk's view.
Scenario runs show the customer's projected annual cost and the supplier's margin per connection for typical household and EV profiles.
painPoints: Marketing prices set in a spreadsheet drift from the portfolio's actual sourcing cost within weeks.
A time-of-use variant with the wrong block boundaries under-recovers cost in exactly the hours demand peaks.

Regulatory disclosure text maintained separately from the product goes stale on the next change.

Exceptions found late are fixed by manual corrections that hurt the straight-through billing rate.

flows.title: Price and Contract a Multi-Site B2B Deal
flows.description: The Portfolio and Trading Manager (port) and Proposition and Pricing Manager (prop) price a multi-site business contract cost-plus from the portfolio position, the Industrial Energy Manager (indm) signs, and the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) activates the sites.
flows.trigger: A business customer with multiple sites requests a supply offer for the coming contract period.
flows.successSignal: All sites are contracted, switched and billed under one framework agreement whose price reflects the portfolio's actual cost.

steps.title: Collect the site list and consumption profiles
keyFacts: Each site is identified by its connection (EAN in the Netherlands, CUPS in Iberia) and its historical interval consumption is pulled from validated meter data.
Profiles are aggregated into a portfolio load shape per 15-minute block that drives the cost-plus calculation.
painPoints: Site lists arrive as spreadsheets with wrong or missing connection identifiers.
Quoting on annual volumes instead of interval profiles misprices peaky industrial load.

steps.title: Build the cost-plus quote from the price curves
keyFacts: The quote prices the load shape against forward curves plus configured components for imbalance, guarantees of origin, grid fees and margin.
The sourcing desk sees the hedge required if the deal is won before the price is sent.
painPoints: A quote priced off yesterday's curve during a volatile week can be loss-making by the time it is accepted.
Imbalance cost left out of the price because it lives in another team's system.

The same component model is used by billing and by the customer trading desk, so a click executed later bills correctly.
painPoints: Bespoke B2B contracts kept in Word documents cannot be billed without manual interpretation.
Options promised by sales that the billing model cannot express become standing corrections.

streams.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streams.description: Take a customer from sign-up to active supply: automated intake, identity and credit check, contract creation and the switch or move-in through market communication (EDSN and the central connection register in the Netherlands, SIPS and distributor ATR files in Iberia), followed by activation and welcome, so that every sign-up becomes a billable connection without manual re-keying.
outcomes: Every sign-up becomes an active supply contract through market communication without manual work
Switches and move-ins complete within the market's lead times, so customers see supply start on the date promised
Rejected or disputed switches are worked as exceptions with full context instead of being discovered at first invoice
One intake and contract model serves Dutch (EDSN, C-AR) and Iberian (SIPS, ATR) processes

flows.title: Switch a Dutch Household to a New Supplier
flows.description: A Household or Business Energy Customer (endc) signs up, the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) oversees the automated intake, register lookup and EDSN switch, and the Customer Service Lead (csrv) owns the welcome.
flows.trigger: A household accepts a proposition on the supplier's website, app or a partner channel.
flows.successSignal: The switch is confirmed by the market, supply starts on the requested date and the customer has a portal account and welcome pack.

steps.title: Sign up in the chosen channel
keyFacts: The sign-up journey is the one configured with the proposition: address, connection, chosen product, payment preference and consents.
Dutch supplier clients of the platform serve more than 7 million households and 3 million business customers, so intake runs at high volume every day.
painPoints: Journeys that ask for the EAN code lose customers who do not know it.
Sign-ups captured in a channel tool and re-keyed later create delays and typos.

steps.title: Verify identity and run the credit check
keyFacts: Identity, address and credit checks run automatically on the intake with configurable acceptance rules per product and customer type.
Outcomes are logged on the customer account for later disputes and regulatory questions.
painPoints: Manual credit checks queue for days and lose the customer to a competitor.
Accepting every customer without checks shows up months later as bad debt.

steps.title: Look up the connection in the central connection register
keyFacts: The address is resolved to its connection in the central connection register so the switch message targets the right EAN and grid operator.

C-AR returns the 18-digit EAN per commodity with grid operator, meter number and type, profile category, capacity code and the current supplier and BRP; these are stored on the connection point for billing and allocation.
painPoints: A wrong EAN produces a switch of the neighbour's connection and a dispute for two households.
Register data not stored locally is looked up again for every downstream process.

steps.title: Create the contract and submit the switch message
keyFacts: The supply contract and connection point are created and the switch or move-in message is sent to the market with the requested start date.

Directive (EU) 2019/944 caps a switch at three weeks; the switch message (leverancierswissel or inhuizing) carries the requested date and the EAN, and the platform processes 20 million connections daily, so message volumes run through automated flows rather than operators.
painPoints: Contracts created before the switch is confirmed bill customers the supplier does not yet supply.
Switch messages hand-built per case are sent late and miss the requested date.

steps.title: Handle rejections and cooling-off cancellations
keyFacts: Rejections (unknown or inactive EAN, a switch already pending on the connection, customer data not matching the register) land in an exception queue with the EDSN reason code and the sign-up context; in the Dutch process the losing supplier cannot block a switch.

A customer who cancels within the 14-day cooling-off period triggers a cancellation message before the effective date; resolved cases are resubmitted automatically, unresolvable ones trigger customer communication.
painPoints: Rejections read from a message log by hand are missed until the customer calls about a missing start.
Working exceptions without the original sign-up context means calling the customer for data already given.

flows.title: Onboard an Iberian Supplier Customer via SIPS and ATR
flows.description: The Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) of a Spanish or Portuguese supplier onboards a customer from CUPS lookup in SIPS, through distributor switching files, to an active contract and first billing cycle on the Nemon-heritage Iberian platform.
flows.trigger: A customer signs a supply contract with a Spanish or Portuguese supplier and provides the CUPS of the supply point.
flows.successSignal: The distributor confirms the change of supplier, the contract is active with the correct access tariff and the first billing cycle runs.

steps.title: Capture the CUPS and consult SIPS
keyFacts: The CUPS (20-22 characters, ES or PT prefix) is validated against the distributor's SIPS to retrieve the access tariff (2.0TD, 3.0TD or 6.xTD), contracted power per period, meter type, current supplier and the distributor responsible.
About 100 suppliers in Spain and Portugal onboard customers through this route on the platform.
painPoints: A mistyped CUPS returns another customer's supply point.
SIPS data consulted once and not stored has to be re-fetched at every billing question.

streams.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streams.description: Turn smart-meter P4 reads, telemetry streams, clustered site data and customer-submitted readings into validated, estimated and plausibility-checked volumes per connection and interval, ready for billing, allocation and consumption analysis; the platform's software validates over 90% of Dutch energy consumption data.
outcomes: Validated, estimated and plausibility-checked volumes exist for every connection and interval before billing and allocation need them
Smart-meter P4, telemetry and clustered data land in one meter-data model regardless of source
Missing or implausible readings are estimated by rule and flagged, never billed silently
Validation keeps its reliability as interval granularity moves to 15-minute blocks

flows.title: Collect and Validate Interval Data for a Billing Period
flows.description: The Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) oversees the automated collection, matching, validation and estimation of meter data for a period, with the Household or Business Energy Customer (endc) submitting readings for non-smart connections.
flows.trigger: The billing calendar reaches the data-collection deadline for a period.
flows.successSignal: Validated volumes are released for every billable connection and interval with estimations and exceptions documented.

steps.title: Receive smart-meter and telemetry data
keyFacts: Daily standard readings arrive through the grid operators' P4 channel for every smart meter; household interval data (15-minute electricity, hourly gas) only where the customer has consented, which dynamic and time-of-use contracts require; telemetry streams cover large-consumer, production and flex-asset meters.
The largest implementation on the platform processes more than 25 million connections, so ingestion is stream-based and idempotent.
painPoints: Files delivered late or twice corrupt the period's volumes when ingestion is not idempotent.
Each provider's format handled by its own script breaks on every format change.

streams.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streams.description: Produce correct invoices from validated volumes and configured contracts: periodic, annual and final billing runs with VAT, energy taxes, guarantees of origin and split invoicing, followed by reconciliation of billed against allocated volumes and traceable corrections, so that the straight-through billing rate rises and the invoice correction rate falls.
outcomes: The straight-through billing rate rises because invoices are produced from validated volumes and configured contracts with no manual step
VAT, guarantees of origin and split invoicing are applied by rule per contract and jurisdiction
Annual and final settlements reconcile billed volumes against allocated volumes, so corrections are rare and explained
Every correction is traceable to its cause (meter, market message, tariff), feeding fewer corrections next run

painPoints: Contracts with mid-period changes handled by hand become the bulk of manual billing work.
Final invoices missed at move-out leave revenue uncollected and customers confused.

steps.title: Price volumes against tariffs, VAT and energy taxes
keyFacts: Volumes are priced per component: supply price (fixed, variable or dynamic per 15-minute block), grid and metering charges passed through, Dutch energy tax in annual brackets per connection with the tax reduction per electricity connection (the ODE levy is part of the energy tax since 2023), Spanish IVA and Impuesto Especial sobre la Electricidad, and VAT at the applicable rate.

Dynamic tariffs rate the customer's consented interval consumption against the EPEX (or OMIE) day-ahead price per block plus the configured mark-up; without interval consent a dynamic contract cannot be billed correctly.
painPoints: Tax rate changes maintained per tenant are applied late in some tenants.
Dynamic products billed on hourly averages misstate cost once the market runs in 15-minute blocks.

outcomes: The portfolio is hedged to the configured strategy so that gross margin per MWh holds through price shocks
Price curves and cost-plus prices are the single source for propositions, B2B quotes and margin tracking
Positions, volumes and value per segment are visible every 15 minutes
Procurement decisions reflect the latest demand forecast rather than last month's spreadsheet

Curves are versioned so that every quote and valuation references the curve it used.
painPoints: Curves updated by hand from broker e-mails are stale and unauditable.
Hourly curves used after the market moved to 15-minute blocks misvalue intraday shape.

flows.trigger: The daily gas nomination cycle starts for the shipper portfolio.
flows.successSignal: Gas nominations are accepted, the within-day position stays within limits and shipping is settled and reported.

steps.title: Forecast gas demand and supply
keyFacts: Gas demand per profile and supply from contracted sources are forecast per gas day with temperature as the main driver.
The gas trading and shipping agreement signed with EBN on 10 September 2024 is the reference case for this flow.
painPoints: Temperature-sensitive demand forecast from monthly averages misses cold snaps.
Supply schedules kept in e-mail are not in the forecast.

dependencies.description: Day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasting for all EAN types including BSP and flex assets.

dependencies.description: Gas position management, trading and shipping nominations.
dependencies.how: Holds the shipper portfolio and contracted supply.

steps.title: Balance the gas position and trade
keyFacts: The gas position per gas day is balanced by trades within the shipper's strategy and limits.
Trades are recorded with delivery point, period and price.
painPoints: Positions balanced without limits become speculative.
Trades not booked before nomination create a mismatch with the TSO.

steps.title: Nominate to the gas TSO
keyFacts: Hourly nominations per network point and shipper code are sent to GTS as Edig@s NOMINT messages for the gas day (06:00-06:00) and re-nominated within-day; the NOMRES confirmations are stored.
Nomination timeliness is measured as for electricity.
painPoints: Gas and electricity nominations in separate tools double the operational risk.
Re-nomination windows missed under manual operation.

keyFacts: GTS publishes the system balance signal and the shipper's portfolio imbalance within-day; corrective re-nominations or TTF trades are made before the shipper becomes a causer in a balancing action.
Alerts fire when the position approaches the shipper's limits.
painPoints: Imbalance discovered after the gas day is settled at penalty prices.
Monitoring in a TSO portal without linkage to the position is reactive.

steps.title: Settle and report shipping

streams.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streams.description: Act on the near real-time position: intraday steering signals, the ETPA trading cycle run as a guaranteed cycle, solar-optimised and flex-asset steering, and ex-post trading opportunities, so that imbalance cost per MWh falls — up to 53% for BRP-as-a-Service portfolios.
outcomes: Imbalance cost per MWh falls, with up to 53% reduction reported for BRP-as-a-Service portfolios
The ETPA trading cycle runs as a guaranteed cycle, not a best-effort desk task
Solar-optimised and flex-asset steering signals act on near real-time position updates
Every steering action is logged with its expected and realised imbalance effect

flows.title: Run the Guaranteed Intraday Trading Cycle
flows.description: The BRP and Balancing Operator (brpo) runs the intraday cycle: near real-time position, intraday re-forecast, expected imbalance and cost, ETPA trades, re-nominations and cycle review.
flows.trigger: The scheduled intraday cycle fires or a position update breaches the steering threshold.
flows.successSignal: The cycle completes within its guaranteed window with trades executed, re-nominations confirmed and the realised imbalance effect logged.

steps.title: Update the near real-time position
keyFacts: Telemetry, latest meter data and nominations update the portfolio position per 15-minute block in near real time.
The position shows contracted, nominated, expected and measured volumes per block.
painPoints: Positions built from yesterday's allocation are blind to today's weather.
Telemetry not linked to the nomination view is looked at but not acted on.

steps.title: Re-forecast intraday
keyFacts: The intraday forecast is refreshed with the latest weather, solar and measured data for the remaining blocks of the day.
Forecast deltas against the day-ahead forecast are shown per block and asset.
painPoints: Intraday forecasts run once in the morning miss the afternoon cloud cover.
Deltas not attributed to assets cannot be steered.

steps.title: Compute expected imbalance and cost
keyFacts: Expected imbalance per ISP is valued against the expected TenneT imbalance price for the regulation state (upward, downward or two-sided) to show the cost of doing nothing versus trading or steering.
Thresholds per portfolio decide when the cycle trades and when it steers assets.
painPoints: Trading every deviation regardless of expected price loses money on transaction cost.
Ignoring imbalance because its price is unknown is the most expensive option.

The cycle is monitored for completion; a missed window is an incident, not a footnote.
painPoints: Manual intraday trading stops at night and on weekends exactly when solar surplus and low demand coincide.
Trades not fed back to the position leave the desk trading the same volume twice.

flows.title: Steer Flex Assets on Solar and Price Signals
flows.description: The Industrial Energy Manager (indm) registers a flexible asset, the BRP and Balancing Operator (brpo) generates and dispatches steering signals and verifies the response, and the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) settles the flex value.
flows.trigger: A flex asset (battery, EV fleet, solar park, curtailable load) is registered with constraints, and the position or price signals a steering opportunity.
flows.successSignal: Assets respond to signals within their constraints, telemetry confirms the response, and the customer is settled for the value delivered.

steps.title: Register the flex asset and its constraints
keyFacts: The asset is registered with capacity, ramp limits, availability windows, state-of-charge rules and the customer's operational constraints.
Constraints are the contract between the customer and the steering desk.
painPoints: Assets steered outside their constraints cause production losses and end the relationship.
Constraints agreed by e-mail are not enforced by the steering engine.

dependencies.description: Per-site consumption analysis, forecast management and flexibility registration.
dependencies.how: Captures asset registration and constraints in the customer's self-service.

dependencies.description: Near real-time position updates, ETPA trading cycle and steering signals.
dependencies.how: Stores the steering constraints per asset.

steps.title: Generate the steering signal
keyFacts: Signals are computed from the expected imbalance, solar forecast and price signals, optimised per asset within constraints.
Solar-optimised steering shifts flexible load or storage into surplus blocks; aFRR-capable assets bid 0.1 MW setpoints in the 4-hour capacity auctions under TenneT's regime of 11 November 2025.
painPoints: Signals based only on price ignore the portfolio's own imbalance.
Generic signals for all assets ignore each asset's constraints.

painPoints: Dispatch by phone or e-mail is too slow for 15-minute blocks.
Unacknowledged signals leave the desk assuming a response that never came.

streams.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streams.description: Get from market messages to settled volumes: the grid operators' allocation per connection and 15-minute ISP verified by a shadow allocation, reconciliation for SMA and TMT connections through the TenneT MMC-Hub under Allocation 2.0, imbalance settlement checks against the E-programme and allocated volumes, cost attribution per segment and BRP compliance reporting.
outcomes: Allocation and reconciliation volumes match the TenneT MMC-Hub exchange under Allocation 2.0 without disputes
Imbalance settlement is checked against nominations and allocated volumes for every settlement period
BRP compliance reporting is produced from settled data, not rebuilt from spreadsheets
Reconciliation deltas feed back into billing corrections and forecast tuning

flows.title: Allocate and Reconcile a Month under Allocation 2.0
flows.description: The BRP and Balancing Operator (brpo) runs allocation and reconciliation for a month, exchanges data with the TenneT MMC-Hub, resolves deltas and hands reconciled volumes to the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo).
flows.trigger: The allocation calendar opens a month for allocation or reconciliation.
flows.successSignal: Allocation and reconciliation volumes are exchanged with the MMC-Hub, deltas are resolved and reconciled volumes are published to billing.

steps.title: Collect allocation inputs per connection
keyFacts: Validated interval data, profile categories, master data and contract assignments are collected per connection for the month.
The platform validates over 90% of Dutch energy consumption data, so the input quality is monitored per grid area.
painPoints: Master-data changes received late assign a connection to the wrong BRP for part of the month.
Inputs assembled from several systems by hand are incomplete.

steps.title: Verify the grid operators' allocation per 15-minute ISP
keyFacts: Grid operators compute the allocation per BRP, supplier, grid area and 15-minute ISP (TMT from telemetry, SMA from smart-meter quarter-hour data, PRO from profile factors) and publish it through EDSN; the platform runs a shadow allocation from its own validated volumes to verify it.
Both the published and the shadow allocation are versioned per run so that later reconciliation can reference the original.
painPoints: Accepting the published allocation without a shadow run pays for a grid operator's error for the whole month.
Unversioned results make reconciliation deltas unexplainable.

Message status and acknowledgements are tracked per exchange.
painPoints: Exchanges done by file upload are late and untraceable.
Format changes at the hub break every tenant when connectors are not centrally maintained.

Accuracy not measured per segment hides a systematic profile error.

streams.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streams.description: Give business customers a trading desk on their supplier's platform: click contracts executed within a framework contract, forecast management, consumption analysis per site and flexible-asset monetisation, with every customer trade reflected in the supplier's portfolio position immediately — the Jules heritage.
outcomes: Business customers execute click trades within their framework contract without a phone call
Consumption analysis and forecasts per site sit next to the trading position
Flexible assets are monetised with clear, contract-based settlement
Supplier desks see customer trades in the portfolio position immediately and hedge back-to-back

flows.title: Execute a Click Trade under a Framework Contract
flows.description: The Industrial Energy Manager (indm) executes a click trade in self-service, the Portfolio and Trading Manager (port) validates and hedges it, and the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) sees it reflected in billing.
flows.trigger: The customer decides to fix a tranche of open volume at the current forward price.
flows.successSignal: The click is validated, confirmed, hedged back-to-back and reflected in the customer's contract, invoice and the portfolio position.

steps.title: Review the open volume and current price
keyFacts: The customer sees contracted, fixed and open volume per delivery period next to the current click price derived from the forward curve plus contracted components.
Price validity and trading windows are shown as configured in the framework contract.
painPoints: Prices quoted by phone during the day are stale by the time the customer decides.
Open volume computed by the customer in a spreadsheet differs from the supplier's.

steps.title: Place the click order

Orders outside trading windows are rejected with the reason.
painPoints: Orders by e-mail create disputes about the price at the time of the order.
Orders accepted outside windows expose the supplier to price moves.

rootGroups.name: Market Entry and Integration Journeys
rootGroups.description: From market-entry scan to live operations and from connectors to a compliant, integrated operation: the expertise-services and market-and-data-foundation journeys that let a new entrant launch in months, a heritage customer consolidate onto one platform, and every tenant absorb a market change once.

streams.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streams.description: Take a new entrant from decision to live operations and an existing operator from heritage platform to one foundation: the five-workstream market-entry scan, ACM and CNMC licensing, operating model, tenant and brand set-up, market roles, BRP as a Service onboarding, implementation, academy training and the consolidation of Ecedo, EBASE, Jules, Gridhub and Nemon customers.
outcomes: A new entrant decides go or no-go on a five-workstream market-entry scan delivered in five weeks
Licences from ACM (8-14 weeks) or CNMC (12-20 weeks) are obtained on a realistic timeline instead of the six-month underestimate most entrants make
Balance responsibility runs from day one through BRP as a Service (portfolios from 40 GWh, tiered MWh pricing)
First customers are live in months on a platform that already speaks the market's messages
Heritage-platform customers consolidate onto the same foundation without losing service

flows.title: Scan, License and Go Live as a New Supplier
flows.description: The New Market Entrant Lead (newe) runs the market-entry scan, licensing and operating-model set-up, the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) connects market roles and onboards the first customers, and the Energy Company Director (exec) signs off training and hand-over.
flows.trigger: A company decides to explore launching a supplier or BRP in the Netherlands or Spain.
flows.successSignal: The entrant holds its licences and market roles, serves its first customers with balance responsibility in place and its team is trained and supported.

steps.title: Run the market-entry scan
keyFacts: The scan covers five workstreams — regulatory scan, competitive overview, operating model, commercial blueprint and roadmap — in five weeks for the Netherlands or Spain.
The output is a go/no-go with a realistic timeline and setup cost per market.
painPoints: Entrants who skip the scan learn the market's rules from their first rejection.
Business cases built on retail prices without imbalance and market-communication cost.

steps.title: Decide and plan the licensing
keyFacts: ACM licensing takes 8-14 weeks, CNMC 12-20 weeks and a dual application 16-20 weeks; most new entrants underestimate the ramp by six months or more.

The licensing plan lists the ACM supply licence, TenneT BRP recognition (or the BRP-as-a-Service contract in its place), the GTS shipper licence, the CNMC registration and the EDSN market-party registration with owners and dates.
painPoints: Licensing started after the platform build delays the launch by a quarter.
Applications with incomplete evidence restart the clock.

streams.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streams.description: Keep the operation compliant and connected: maintained connectors for EDSN and the central connection register, the TenneT MMC-Hub and nomination interfaces, ETPA, OMIE and REE/SIPS, plus ERP and accounting, payment providers, meter-data providers and the open API, so that market changes ship to every tenant once and integration failures surface as exceptions rather than data loss.
outcomes: Every market message (EDSN, C-AR, MMC-Hub, TenneT, ETPA, OMIE, REE/SIPS) is processed by a maintained connector, so a market change ships to all tenants once
ERP, accounting, payment and meter-data providers are integrated through the open API with monitored delivery
Regulatory changes such as Allocation 2.0 and the 15-minute day-ahead market land on schedule across every tenant
Integration failures surface as workflow exceptions with retry, not as silent data loss

flows.title: Roll Out a Market Change across Every Tenant
flows.description: The Energy Company Director (exec) of a client sees a market change analysed, the Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) and BRP and Balancing Operator (brpo) validate the updated connectors and processing, and the change is released to all tenants.
flows.trigger: A market change is announced, such as Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 (1 January 2025), the 15-minute day-ahead market (30 September 2025) or aFRR 0.1 MW setpoints and 4-hour capacity auctions (11 November 2025).
flows.successSignal: Every tenant processes the new message formats and market rules from the effective date with no tenant-specific patches.

steps.title: Analyse the market change and its impact
keyFacts: The change is analysed against message formats, data model, processing rules and reporting; the impact per tenant and module is listed.

Dutch 2025 changes: Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 on 1 January, 15-minute day-ahead products on 30 September (an SDAC-wide change, so OMIE as well), aFRR 0.1 MW setpoints and 4-hour capacity auctions on 11 November.
painPoints: Each supplier analysing the same change separately multiplies the cost across the market.
Impact missed in reporting surfaces as a compliance incident.

flows.description: The Billing and Operations Manager (bilo) connects a supplier's ERP and payment provider through the open API, maps postings and payment status, tests end to end and monitors exceptions.
flows.trigger: A supplier wants invoices posted to its ERP and SEPA direct debits executed through its bank or payment provider.
flows.successSignal: Postings, direct debits and payment status flow both ways with reconciled totals and exceptions handled in the workflow.

steps.title: Register the integration and credentials
keyFacts: The integration is registered per tenant with credentials, scopes, endpoints and the owner responsible for it.
Credentials are isolated per tenant and rotated per policy.
painPoints: Shared credentials across tenants are a data-isolation breach waiting to happen.
Integrations without an owner are nobody's problem when they fail.
